title: Hairpin lace baby blanket
subtitle: A soft loopy baby blanket made from joined hairpin lace strips in DK weight.
excerpt: Multiple hairpin lace strips joined side by side build a rectangular baby blanket with a loopy, tactile surface. DK weight yarn on a 7 cm frame gives a fabric that is soft and open without being too airy for a baby wrap.
sourceNotes: Hairpin lace blankets using multiple joined strips are a classic domestic crochet format. This strip count, frame width, and finishing border are original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet technique where yarn is looped around a U-shaped metal frame while a central chain is worked with a hook, producing a strip of looped fabric on each side.
A U-shaped metal or plastic tool with two parallel prongs held apart by a connector bar. The spacing of the prongs sets the width of the lace strip.
A crochet row that links the loops from two adjacent hairpin lace strips together, creating a flat seam between them.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 loops per 10 cm of strip length on a 7 cm wide frame in DK weight.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Baby blanket approximately 70 cm wide x 90 cm long.

set 7 cm wide. Six strips joined side by side reach approximately 70 cm across. Each strip runs the full 90 cm length of the blanket.

items.name: DK weight yarn, washable wool or cotton blend

content.text: Work each strip with 1 double crochet through the central loops, rotating the frame after each stitch. Each strip needs 126 loops per side (90 cm at 14 loops per 10 cm). Make 6 strips in total.
Lay two strips side by side. Work a
picking up one loop from each strip per stitch and working 1 double crochet. Join all 6 strips in sequence. Keep the joining rows to an even tension throughout.

Work 2 rounds of double crochet around the whole blanket, turning the corners with 3 double crochets into each corner loop. This stabilises the edges and frames the loopy centre. Weave in all ends securely with your tapestry needle before washing.
